I am 76 years old and I have farmed this 4.1 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves because hired labor costs money we don't have. We are lucky to have well water, but pumping costs electricity, so I count every irrigation.

My land is in two pieces. About 3 mu I keep for wheat and then maize, back to back every year. The other 1.1 mu I plant cotton for cash.

The wheat is already in the ground from last October. I sowed improved Jimai seed at about 15 kg per mu. Before sowing I had the tractor run the rotary tiller, and I put down base fertilizer — 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. Now in spring, I will top-dress the wheat with urea: 80 jin per mu total, half when the wheat greens up in March and half at jointing in April. All together that is about 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 5 kg phosphorus and 4 kg potassium from the base and top dress. I will irrigate three times from my well: once in March when the wheat wakes up, once at jointing in April, and once at flowering in May. I spray herbicide once in early spring for weeds, and if I see aphids I spray insecticide once more. Last year I got 430 kg per mu. This year I expect 450 kg per mu if the frost stays away.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I immediately plant hybrid maize. I buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed from the dealer — everyone around here uses hybrid now, and I saw Old Wang's field last summer, his ears were big and full. I use 2.5 kg seed per mu. After wheat harvest I have the tractor rotary till fast and sow right away. I put 50 jin compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then top dress with 50 jin urea at jointing. That gives about 15 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once after sowing if the soil is dry, and once at tasseling in late July. I spray herbicide right after sowing, and once for corn borer. I expect 500 kg per mu.

For cotton on 1.1 mu, I plough deep in April because cotton likes loose, deep soil. I plant improved Lumianyan seed at 1.5 kg per mu. I put down 60 jin compound fertilizer and 40 jin urea per mu, which comes to about 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium. I learned from the input dealer that cotton needs more potassium, so I buy compound fertilizer with a bit more K. I irrigate three times: at flowering, at peak boll, and once in August if it doesn't rain. Cotton pests are bad here — bollworm, aphids, mites — so I spray four times. I expect 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Every bag of fertilizer is real money. On 4.1 mu I cannot afford waste. But I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. When I am unsure, I watch what Old Wang and the others do, and I do the same. Change is risky.
